facts.statement: The genus Brachyosteus was described by Jaeckel in 1927.
The species Brachyosteus dietrichi was described by Gross in 1932.
Brachyosteus lived during the Late Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Brachyosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Late Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Brachyosteus have been found in Bad Wildungen, Germany.
facts.quote: Fossils are found from Bad Wildungen, Germany.

facts.statement: Brachyosteus is classified as an extinct arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Brachyosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: Brachyosteus belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi.
facts.quote: Brachyosteus is a member of the family Selenosteidae of the clade Aspinothoracidi

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Brachyosteus as Trematosteidae.
Brachyosteus is classified in the class Placodermi.
Brachyosteus lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)
